_doc: Labelled citation-drift pairs for validating wiki.citation_drift.ModelDriftJudge. Each case: a SYNTHESIS (compiled claim) + the SOURCES it was compiled from + the ground-truth `drifted` label + the drift `kind`. Used by tests/test_wiki_citation_drift_judge_live.py to measure the judge prompt's recall (catches real drift) and precision (no false alarms) against DRIFT_RECALL_FLOOR / DRIFT_PRECISION_FLOOR. Judge against the sources ONLY; labels reflect what the sources support, not outside knowledge. Balanced: ~half drifted, ~half faithful, plus edge cases.

cases.synthesis: Vector search always outperforms keyword search for retrieval.
sources: On our LongMemEval-S runs, hybrid vector+keyword search beat keyword-only at k=10.
For rare tokens and exact IDs, keyword (BM25) still outranks pure vector search.

cases.synthesis: The auth service uses RS256 JWTs with a 15-minute access-token TTL and rotates signing keys weekly.
sources: We chose RS256 for JWT signing so the public key can verify without sharing the secret.
Access tokens expire after 15 minutes; refresh tokens after 30 days.

cases.synthesis: The embedder runs as an external HTTP service that must be started before m3.
sources: The BGE-M3 embedder is bundled and runs in-process from a GGUF; no external service or API key is needed.
An optional EMBED_BASE_URL fallback to Ollama/LM Studio exists but is not required.

cases.synthesis: Chatlog turns are stored in the main agent_memory.db under type='chat_log'.
sources: Originally chatlog shared the main DB (type='chat_log' rows in agent_memory.db).
As of the split-store migration, chatlog turns live in a separate agent_chatlog.db; the main DB no longer receives new chat_log rows.

cases.synthesis: Retrieval hits the correct session as the #1 result over 99% of the time.
sources: The correct session is the #1 result for about 92% of questions.
Session-hit-rate @ k=10 is 99.2%; @ k=20 it is 100%.

cases.synthesis: m3 stores memory locally in SQLite and can also run on PostgreSQL as the primary store.
sources: By default, memory lives in a local SQLite file on your hardware.
You can run m3 with PostgreSQL as the primary store via M3_DB_BACKEND=postgres and M3_PRIMARY_PG_URL.

cases.synthesis: The storage seam abstracts SQL differences so the same code runs on SQLite and PostgreSQL.
sources: The dialect seam maps each SQLite construct (placeholders, INSERT OR IGNORE, JSON functions, PRAGMA) to its PostgreSQL equivalent.
A caller asks the dialect for the fragment it needs; the dialect knows the target backend.
Divergent SQL methods are abstract so a new backend fails loud rather than inheriting the wrong SQL.

cases.synthesis: GDPR erasure in m3 purges by explicit enumeration, not only by cascade.
sources: gdpr_forget purges the subject's rows by explicit enumeration across the relevant tables and does not rely on ON DELETE CASCADE alone.

cases.synthesis: Full-text search is native on both backends: FTS5 bm25 on SQLite and a tsvector GIN index on PostgreSQL.
sources: SQLite keyword search uses FTS5 with bm25 ranking.
On PostgreSQL, files_search uses a generated tsvector column with a GIN index, queried with @@ to_tsquery and ranked by ts_rank.

cases.synthesis: The wiki citation-drift check is report-only.
sources: The citation-drift check writes a lint section listing possibly-drifted syntheses.
It never auto-supersedes, never sets a verdict, and never mutates a row; remediation is a human act.

cases.synthesis: The banner was clobbered because the release pipeline regenerates it from a stale source asset.
sources: The banner was updated directly on GitHub main.
An in-flight feature branch, cut before that edit, still carried the old banner and overwrote it when it merged and released.

cases.synthesis: The coalesce cache was renamed to avoid a table-name collision with the core resolution cache.
sources: entity_coalesce's embedding cache was named entity_embeddings, the same table as core migration 032's resolution cache, with incompatible columns.
It was renamed entity_coalesce_embeddings (module prefix) so the two subsystems stop sharing a name.
